title: Euphoria
synopsis: You're 20 in East Highland, two years into recovery, working a coffee shop with a sponsor on speed dial. Tonight's meeting is the first you've gone to alone. The town has not gotten quieter.

nodes.text: Church basement. Cheap coffee. You sit on a folding chair early, headphones in. People begin filing in. You see a face you do not want to see: Cassie.

choices.text: Stay; recovery is bigger than your discomfort
choices.consequence: Hold the line.

choices.text: Step outside for one minute
choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Reset.

nodes.text: She approaches. She is sober too, surprisingly, and she looks like she has cried already today. She says, 'Can we talk after?' You haven't spoken in two years.

choices.text: Agree to talk
choices.consequence: You commit to “Agree to talk.” The story records the instinct as “Practice” and carries it forward.

choices.text: Say 'maybe' and see how the hour goes
choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Triage—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: On the sidewalk you call your sponsor — Ali, who picks up on the second ring even on Tuesdays. He listens. He says, 'You're already doing the work by calling. Go back inside.'

choices.text: Go back inside steadily
choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Trust him—follows you into whatever comes next.

choices.text: Stay outside for the meeting
choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Slow.

nodes.text: You share, briefly, that this is your first meeting alone. The room is warm. An older woman named Marsha says 'glad you're here' in the exact way you needed.

choices.text: Stay for fellowship after
choices.consequence: Build the room.

choices.text: Slip out quickly
choices.consequence: There is no taking “Slip out quickly” back. Save energy shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Cassie's sister Lexi is at the meeting too, in the back, surprising you both. She catches your eye and gives a small, kind nod. The Howard sisters have, somehow, both ended up in this room.

choices.text: Talk to Lexi first
choices.consequence: You commit to “Talk to Lexi first.” The story records the instinct as “Easier first” and carries it forward.

choices.text: Talk to both sisters at once
choices.consequence: You commit to “Talk to both sisters at once.” The story records the instinct as “Be brave” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: You, Lexi, Cassie, and Marsha sit at a diner counter at 10 p.m. and order pancakes. Cassie cries quietly into hers. Nobody comments. Lexi reaches over and squeezes her hand.

choices.text: Tell Cassie you're glad she's sober
choices.consequence: You commit to “Tell Cassie you're glad she's sober.” The story records the instinct as “Generous” and carries it forward.

choices.text: Tell Lexi you're glad she's here too
choices.consequence: You commit to “Tell Lexi you're glad she's here too.” The story records the instinct as “Equal” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Wednesday morning. The coffee shop. Your manager Fez is, somehow, kind of a manager now. He gives you the morning shift on purpose so the rest of the day is yours.

choices.text: Tell Fez about the meeting
choices.consequence: “Tell Fez about the meeting” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Trust him.

choices.text: Stay quiet at work and write later
choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Compartmentalize.

nodes.text: You keep a notebook. You write the sentence: 'I went to a meeting alone and I came home alone and I did not use.' You read it three times. You realize you have started, slowly, to believe in yourself.

choices.text: Buy a second notebook for the year
choices.consequence: Build the practice.

choices.text: Start texting one line a day to Ali
choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Accountability.

nodes.text: Jules is in town for the week. The first phone call is tentative. The second is honest. The third is, in some way you can't yet name, possible.

choices.text: See her
choices.consequence: There is no taking “See her” back. Try shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

choices.text: Wait to see her until you've talked to Ali
choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Discipline.

nodes.text: Your mom watches you make her coffee in the morning. She does not say much. She doesn't have to. She has, you realize, been working as hard as you, for longer.

choices.text: Tell her you love her plainly
choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Plain.

choices.text: Cook her breakfast in return
choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Action.

nodes.text: Your sister Gia is in high school now. She watches you the way she used to watch the front door at 3 a.m. You realize she is not yet sure you will not relapse. You realize her patience is also love.

choices.text: Take Gia somewhere fun on Saturday
choices.consequence: You commit to “Take Gia somewhere fun on Saturday.” The story records the instinct as “Show up” and carries it forward.

choices.text: Apologize directly for the years
choices.consequence: “Apologize directly for the years” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Speak.

nodes.text: Two years. Marsha hands you a chip. You almost don't take it because chips have, in the past, felt like jinxes. You take it. You squeeze it in your hand the whole drive home.

choices.text: Pin it on your fridge
choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Visible.

choices.text: Carry it in your pocket every day
choices.consequence: There is no taking “Carry it in your pocket every day” back. Private shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Fez tells you he's opening a small bakery. He wants you as the manager. The hours are hard. The job is real. You realize you have been offered, of all things, a future.

choices.text: Accept the job
choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Build.

choices.text: Negotiate fewer hours so you can keep writing
choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Balance—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: Six months later the bakery opens. You and Fez and Marsha and Lexi and your mom and Gia are there. There is a small cake. Marsha gives a small speech. Fez almost cries. You almost cry.

choices.text: Take a photo for the year
choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Mark it—follows you into whatever comes next.

choices.text: Just be there
choices.consequence: “Just be there” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Be there.

nodes.text: You write — not a book, exactly, but a small collection of essays. You publish one in a magazine. The piece, more than the bakery or the job, makes you feel like a person with a project.

choices.text: Send the essay to Jules
choices.consequence: “Send the essay to Jules” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Share.

choices.text: Send it to your sponsor
choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Share.

nodes.text: Jules replies in a long email. She says she's proud of you. She says she's not in a place to come home. She says she'd like to keep writing. You realize, slowly, that not all loves are reunions. Some are just letters.

choices.text: Accept the letters as enough
choices.consequence: There is no taking “Accept the letters as enough” back. Mature shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

choices.text: Plan to visit her in a year, no pressure
choices.consequence: You commit to “Plan to visit her in a year, no pressure.” The story records the instinct as “Patient” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Ali, who is dying — you don't know it yet, you'll find out next month — sends you back a one-line text: 'You're writing the version of yourself the rest of us can read.' You frame it.

choices.text: Visit Ali in person next weekend
choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Show up.

choices.text: Send him a long thank-you letter
choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Letter.

nodes.text: Five years. You give the chip back at a meeting you sponsor a teenager from. You realize you are now Marsha. You realize this is, finally, a story without an exit.

choices.text: Stay in East Highland
choices.consequence: “Stay in East Highland” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Place.

choices.text: Move; keep the meetings the same
choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Travel—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: Gia graduates high school. You give the speech at the family dinner. You say plain things. Your mom cries. Gia hugs you longer than usual. You go to bed sober and full and tired in the right way.

choices.text: Keep building the small life
choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Maintain.

choices.text: Travel for the first time in your life
choices.consequence: You commit to “Travel for the first time in your life.” The story records the instinct as “Reward yourself” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Ali is gone. You sit in the meeting in the chair he used to sit in. The room is the same. You are the same and very different. You decide what to do with the rest of the year.

choices.text: Hold the chair in East Highland
choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Steady—follows you into whatever comes next.

choices.text: Take meetings on the road
choices.consequence: “Take meetings on the road” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Mobile.

nodes.text: You stay. The town gets a little kinder, year over year. You sponsor four people over a decade. Two of them stay sober. Two of them don't. You learn that the score isn't the point. The room is the point.

You travel. Meetings everywhere, surprisingly, work the same way. You write essays from cafés in cities you used to dream about as a teenager. You realize that recovery is portable. So, finally, are you.
